quote.text: the contrivances by which Orchids are fertilised, are as varied and almost as perfect as any of the most beautiful adaptations in the animal kingdom
quote.author: Charles Darwin, On the Various Contrivances by which British and Foreign Orchids are Fertilised by Insects (John Murray, 1862), Introduction, p. 1

stories.headline: Audio-Technica began selling its Kiso-cypress flagship headphone on 6 November
stories.dek: The price is US$3,799, a figure Audio-Technica’s own page does not carry. Major HiFi’s review lists “Vocals can sound hollow and distant” among the cons.

stories.headline: Michael Hassler’s checklist counted 31,090 wild orchid species on 29 October
stories.dek: A query against the GBIF backbone returns 33,355; the count in general reference is about 28,000. The American Orchid Society, which judges all of them, has close to 10,000 members, down from 29,000 in 2001.

stories.headline: Singapore Airlines committed S$2 billion to four new long-haul cabins
stories.dek: The unveiling at Marina Bay Sands on 6 November booked a further S$130 million for SilverKris lounge work worldwide, Changi included. Service entry has now slipped twice, to the second half of 2027.

stories.headline: Dublin names Europe’s Ukraine negotiators: Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland
stories.dek: António Costa announced the five-state team at 9.15 on Friday night. Two days of talks in Abu Dhabi produced one agreement: a prisoner swap of over a thousand a side.

stories.headline: Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency says reported incidents have tripled since September
stories.dek: The Cyber Security Agency said on Friday the attacks are not a coordinated campaign against Singapore. A day earlier the Health Ministry named six breached healthcare entities.

stories.headline: Molloy & Sons prints the spec sheet luxury blanket mills omit
stories.dek: The Donegal weaver gives fibre, size and weight at €195. Begg x Co publishes none of the three at £3,550, and Johnstons of Elgin none at £1,995.

stories.headline: Anthropic prices its Nasdaq listing on 18 November after opening UK retail
stories.dek: Amendment No. 2 offers 825 million shares at US$70 to US$78. Four prospectuses filed on 12 November added retail buyers in Britain, the EEA, Japan and Australia.

stories.headline: Apple put HomeView on sale in Singapore on Friday at S$399
stories.dek: Singapore is one of seven launch countries; the European Union is not one of them. Consumer Reports calls the device “essentially a $300 iPhone accessory that plugs into a wall”.

stories.headline: Gold Derby forecasts Johnny Depp’s Ebenezer to end Godzilla Minus Zero’s run
stories.dek: Box Office Mojo’s opening figure has finally stopped moving at $30,628,265 after three revisions. Wikipedia still prints the first one.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Anxious Cohort
stories.headline: Understanding Society finds emotional problems more than doubled among British 12-year-olds
stories.dek: The European Journal of Epidemiology published the fifteen-year series on 11 November: 10.1 per cent in 2009, 25.4 in 2024 — and conduct problems falling throughout.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The December Meeting
stories.headline: Futures price a December Federal Reserve rise at 100 per cent
stories.dek: The Bureau of Labor Statistics put producer prices 6.5 per cent higher over twelve months, the most since November 2022. The ten-year breakeven moved one basis point.

stories.headline: A pre-registered Oslo-led trial finds mouth exercises do not ease sleep apnoea
stories.dek: The Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine published it on 10 November: 104 adults, three sleep-lab nights each, and a difference of 0.6 events an hour.

stories.headline: ART SG closes its early-bird tickets at midnight on 24 November
stories.dek: Two Saturday passes cost S$44 instead of S$88, and a child of 16 or under walks in free with a ticketed adult at Marina Bay Sands in January.

stories.headline: Kazakhstan’s Prime Minister disclosed 463,829 applications for an irrevocable betting self-ban
stories.dek: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov disclosed the figure in June. Separately, 5.1 million Kazakhstanis have switched off their own ability to borrow.
